transcript.text:
Thank you all for the clear constraints. Let me walk through how I plan to reconcile everything before publishing the binding plan.

First, the command net: Capt. Mercer's directive requires command on C2 from 0600 to 1000. I'll honor that. After 1000, command reverts to C1 per the standard plan.

Second, logistics: SFC Alvarez, R3 is the only repeater with sufficient battery for the logistics yard, and it must run at low power from 0700 to 1100. Since C2 is being used for command during 0600-1000, logistics will need a fallback channel during that overlap. I'll keep logistics on C2 as primary outside the command window, but during 0700-1000 when both command and logistics need capacity and R3 is at low power, I'll assign logistics to C1 as a fallback to avoid overloading R3 on C2. After 1000, logistics returns to C2 on R3 at low power until 1100, then resumes normal configuration.

Third, clinic support: WO1 Patel, R1 goes offline 1200-1400 for firmware validation. Clinic support normally uses C3, and R2 covers the clinic area. During the 1200-1400 outage, clinic support will shift to R2. That's consistent since R2 already covers the clinic area.

Fourth, airfield: 1LT Brooks, C4 is unavailable at the airfield, so airfield services will use C3 at 25 watts with an interference check completed before 0800. Since your requirement is tied to pre-0800 calibration and you've confirmed no information about C3 airfield usage extending past 0800, I'll plan C3 airfield services as a pre-0800 activity. That means there's no overlap with the 1200-1400 clinic fallback on R2. However, I do need to confirm with you: is any airfield services traffic on C3 expected to continue past 0800? If not, the plan is clean. If yes, we'll need to deconflict C3 on R2 for both clinic and airfield during 1200-1400.

1LT Brooks, can you confirm whether any C3 airfield traffic continues past 0800? Once I have that confirmation, I'll publish the binding plan and get the signal shop configured before 1800 today.
